sentences.text: The petitioners in WP No. 147069/2020 are the absolute owners of the land bearing R.S.No.128/3A measuring 2 acres 20 guntas situated at Gadag.
2. The petitioners in WP No.147610/2020 are the absolute owners of the land bearing R.S.No.128/3B measuring 2 acres 20 guntas situated at Gadag.

3. Respondent No.1 issued a preliminary notification dated 13.11.2012 under Section 15 of the Karnataka State Highways Act, 1964 (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') for the purpose of Gadag bypass and an extent of 16 guntas in each in R.S.Nos.128/3A and 128/3B belonging to the petitioners were proposed for 16 guntas 8 annas.
4.
Respondent No.1 fixed the market value at Rs.874/- per square feet.
Thereafter on 20.08.2014 respondent No.3 fixed the market value of the acquired land at Rs.1,093/- per square feet by treating it as commercial land.
The petitioners had allegedly entered into an agreement accepting the market value fixed by respondent No.1.
5. Respondent No.1 prepared spot panchanama dated 08.04.2015 stating that the petitioners have established ginning factory on the subject land.
Respondent No.6 issued a communication dated 22.04.2015 to respondent No.2 stating that the subject land can be treated as non-agricultural land.

The project Co-Ordinator on 13.04.2017 communicated to respondent No.2 stating that there is 12 meter width excess NC: 2024:KHC-D:4512 road between R.S.Nos.128/3A and 128/3B and accordingly, respondent No.2 issued an endorsement to respondent No.1 on 27.04.2017 stating that as per records, 12 meters road is left by the petitioners providing access to their respective lands.

Thereafter respondent No.1 issued a modified notification under Section 19 of the Act, modifying the extent of land to be acquired from the petitioners as 10 guntas instead of 16 guntas and 10 annas in R.S.Nos.128/3A and 128/3B were shown as Government road.

Respondent No.1 passed an award determining the compensation payable to the petitioners to an extent of 10 guntas each at Rs.874/-
per square feet.
The petitioners request with respondent No.2 to grant compensation to the entire extent of 16 guntas 8 annas was not acceded.
Therefore, this petition.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the sale deed at annexure-A and the revenue records clearly establish that 16 guntas 8 annas of land in R.S.Nos.128/3A and 128/3B exclusively belongs to the petitioners and it does not belong to the Government and the award is passed granting compensation to an extent of 10 guntas solely on the ground that the petitioners have left 6 Jyoti.S.Malladad vs Special Land Acquisition Officer on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62183011/
5 guntas each in the respective lands for providing access road to their respective lands and treated the same as Government land.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioners have been deprived of the compensation to which they are legally entitled to, and the impugned award passed is in violation of Article 300A of the Constitution.

Learned High Court Government Pleader for the State would submit that on spot inspection, it was found an extent of 6 guntas each in the petitioners land was utilized for the purpose of providing access road to the adjacent land and therefore, the respondents have rightly determined the compensation to an extent of 10 guntas 8 annas by treating it as Government land.

He further submitted that the compensation has been awarded by treating the subject land as commercial land and therefore, the compensation awarded to the petitioners is just and proper, and does not warrant any interference by this Court.
8. I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.

9. The sale deed at Annexure-A and the record of rights annexed to the petition indicated that the petitioners have purchased an extent of 2 acres 20 guntas of land in R.S.Nos.128/3A and 128/3B respectively.
The sale deed further indicated that on the western eastern portion of the land, 50 feet width road is left for providing access to the adjacent land.
The panchanama annexed to the petition indicated that the petitioners have established ginning factory on the subject land and the subject lands have been treated as commercial lands.

However, based on the communication issued by the project Co-Ordinator, an extent of 6 guntas each belonging to the petitioners has been treated as Government road only on the ground that the said extent of land was utilized for the purpose of providing access of adjacent land.
The extent of 6 guntas each was utilized for providing access road to their respective lands, and the extent of land utilized for providing access is not for the public at large.
It is also not disputed that the said extent of land utilized for providing access to adjacent lands belongs to the petitioner.

In the absence of any material to establish that the said extent of land vested with the Government or belongs to Government, the determination of the compensation by taking the extent of land as 10 guntas instead of 16 guntas 8 acres is arbitrary and discriminatory.
10.
Initially the price fixation committee had determined the market value in respect of the subject land at Rs.874/- per square feet by treating it as commercial land.
Thereafter the market value was revised by the price fixation committee on 20.08.2014 at annexure-D at Rs.1,093/- square feet.
The respondents under the impugned award without considering the revised market value has determined the compensation at Rs.874/- instead of Rs.1,093/-.

Therefore, the impugned modified notification dated 20.05.2017 issued under Section 19 of the Act and the award dated 26.08.2019 passed by respondent No.1 are not sustainable in law and the same requires to be quashed.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Jyoti.
